title: Deferred Prefill Affinity Controller with Empirical Acceptance Calibrator
creator: Priya Anand
description: Introduce a deferred-prefill affinity controller that routes early prefill work to candidate model kernels based on a lightweight kernel-fit score and a small empirical acceptance calibrator. The goal is to enable optimistic decode handoffs with measurable acceptance probability and an automated safe fallback sequence when acceptance confidence is low.
background: We currently support speculative decode paths via probe-prefill and optimistic handoff, but routing decisions are coarse and often misroute prefill work to kernels with poor attention alignment resulting in degraded acceptance and higher rollback rates. Kernel selection today considers static heuristics (model size, quant) but not recent attention profile or KV cache affinity. This ticket designs runtime machinery to defer committing a prefill to a handoff until an empirical acceptance signal is available and to bias routing toward kernels with demonstrated affinity for recent request distributions.
proposal: Build an affinity controller that computes a transient kernel-fit score per incoming prefill. Score inputs: recent attention window shape (avg attention span), kv-cache hit locality, sequence length histogram, and micro-benchmark of kernel per-token latency. Use a lightweight empirical acceptance calibrator that runs a micro-decode probe (<=4 tokens) on candidate kernels to estimate acceptance probability. Only commit the handoff if acceptance probability exceeds a configurable threshold; otherwise fall back to local decode. Maintain per-kernel short-term statistics and decay them over a time constant to adapt to workload drift.
implementation_steps: Design kernel-fit score: define features, normalization, and decay semantics
Implement micro-probe harness: safe sandboxed <=4 token probe with strict time budget
Affinity controller service: in-runtime module to score candidates and schedule probes
Acceptance calibrator: logistic regression model trained online from probe outcomes
Fallback machinery: safe rollback path to local decode with KV cache merge strategy
Telemetry and dashboard: acceptance rate, probe latency, fallback frequency, per-kernel fit
E2E tests: load tests that simulate attention profile shift and ensure graceful degrade
Canary rollout: small traffic fraction with detailed tracing and kill-switch
acceptance_criteria: P95 user-visible latency increase <= 5% compared to baseline when controller enabled
Acceptance probability calibration: predicted vs observed acceptance error <= 5 percentage points
Fallback rate <= 2% under steady-state traffic; under adversarial attention shifts fallback increases but remains < 10%
No unnoticed correctness regressions (validated by regression eval set for top-10 customer prompts)
Observability: charts for per-kernel fit score, probe success rate, and rollout breakpoint
fallback_playbook: If probe times out: abort handoff and route request to local decode path; increment 'probe_timeout' counter
If acceptance probability < threshold: perform local decode with KV stitching and record 'forced_local'
If kernel mis-accepts (produces divergent output): increment misaccept counter and mark kernel for soft-retirement for 10 minutes
If fallback rate > 10% for 5m: auto-disable controller via runtime feature flag and alert SRE
rollback_plan: Feature flag gating with immediate kill-switch; maintain ability to route all traffic to baseline (no controller) within 30s. Track last-known-good controller config and return to it automatically if misbehavior is detected.
risks: Probe overhead increases CPU/GPU utilization if micro-probes are too frequent
Acceptance calibrator may overfit to early traffic and mis-estimate under distribution shift
KV stitching complexity can introduce correctness edge cases when merging partial caches
Complexity increases observability surface and runbook demands
tradeoffs: Probe depth vs confidence: deeper probes raise confidence but add latency/cost
Aggressive affinity biasing vs exploration: favoring high-fit kernels reduces fallbacks but can mask drift
Online calibrator simplicity vs expressivity: prefer lightweight model to keep runtime overhead low
decisions: Use <=4 token micro-probes for acceptance estimation
Store per-kernel fit stats with exponential decay (tau=10 minutes)
Acceptance probability threshold default 0.85, configurable per-customer tier
KV stitching implemented as last-writer-wins with deterministic ordering to avoid nondeterminism

2026-03-02 Marcus Linde: prototyped kernel-fit extractor locally. Observed that 'avg attention span' and 'kv-affinity' are predictive of probe acceptance (AUC 0.78). Need to test under multi-tenant noise.

2026-03-03 Leah Wong: micro-probe harness validated on dev cluster; 95th percentile probe latency 12ms with 4-token probes. Next steps: integrate exponential decay state store and wire telemetry counters.

2026-03-03 Product review: PM requests a per-customer toggle and a less aggressive default threshold for P1 customers. Also requests a plan to surface misaccepts to Customer Success for early detection.
notes: This approach intentionally defers committing to a handoff until a small empirical signal is available. It aims to reduce rollback churn and improve end-to-end per-token cost by avoiding wasted speculative decode work.
If successful, affinity controller metrics should enable smarter long-lived kernel placement decisions and better autoscaling signals for Dedicated pools.
